title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is a typed sheet, photographed upside down, headed 'NA 27' and dated 8 May 1986. It contains three addenda keyed to page numbers of Récoltes et Semailles: p.1074, p.1076 and p.1088, all in ReS IV, the part on the 'Burial' and the 'Mebkhout affair' around the Riemann–Hilbert correspondence for D-modules.

(1) Note to p.1074. Grothendieck explains that 'du cru de Kashiwara' referred to the incident at the Goulaouic–Schwartz seminar as reported to him by Mebkhout. He says he no longer has reason to believe Kashiwara acted incorrectly on that occasion. He still holds that other acts of appropriation by Kashiwara and some collaborators, described elsewhere in ReS, deserve to be called 'escroqueries'. He records that he sent Kashiwara a copy of ReS IV right after printing. On 9 February 1986 he followed it with a letter of apology for having echoed the distortions in Mebkhout's version. He has had no reply.

(2) Note to p.1076. He withdraws an unfavourable prejudice against Kashiwara. Until about 1979–80, nobody understood the place and scope of the result (the Riemann–Hilbert correspondence). Kashiwara, who first sensed it, probably understood it no less than the others, perhaps even Mebkhout himself. He has deleted the end of a sentence after 'Verdier en personne', which was even more disobliging to Kashiwara and equally unjustified.

(3) Note to p.1088. He now calls Mebkhout's version 'affabulatoire', which drastically changes 'my presuppositions' about the seminar incident. He still finds his general reflections pertinent: collective abdication before the degradation of scientific ethics feeds extreme conflicts such as Mebkhout vs. Kashiwara.

The sheet sits in the middle of the July 1986 'ateliers' manuscript, between lattice and Boolean-algebra computations. The neighbouring pages are p.107, with a lattice diagram on subsets of I, and p.108–109, a lemma on disjoint families e_i generating a Boolean subalgebra.

ideas.what: Retraction/softening of accusations against Kashiwara regarding priority on the Riemann–Hilbert correspondence; Mebkhout's account called 'affabulatoire'
ideas.modern_name: History of the Riemann–Hilbert correspondence (Kashiwara 1980/84; Mebkhout 1980/84) and the ReS priority dispute
ideas.where_published: Possibly among later notes/errata to Récoltes et Semailles; the ReS IV text it modifies is published

missed.claim: Dated (8 May 1986) documentary evidence that Grothendieck retracted part of his ReS accusations against Kashiwara. He judged Mebkhout's account of the Goulaouic–Schwartz seminar incident 'affabulatoire', deleted a disobliging passage, and had sent Kashiwara an apology letter on 9 Feb 1986. He nevertheless maintained other charges of 'escroqueries'.
missed.quote: Je rappelle que c'est là la version de Mebkhout, qui à présent m'apparaît comme affabulatoire.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Secondary accounts of the Riemann–Hilbert priority dispute usually rely on the ReS text as written in 1985. This addendum shows Grothendieck himself partly revised his view of Kashiwara's role. That is relevant for fair attribution and for the history of D-module theory.

deep.surprise_reason: No mathematics. It is historically notable that Grothendieck explicitly called Mebkhout's account fabricated and apologized to Kashiwara, which is not widely cited. It may, however, be known from errata or circulated notes to ReS.
transcription_corrections: Page is photographed upside down; the transcription order is correct.
'[-dux-] cru' is 'du cru' with a typing overstrike.
The handwritten insertion near 'déformations' reads approximately 'sans réserves', apparently qualifying the apology ('lettre d'excuses sans réserves').
'au sujet des certains faits' should read 'au sujet de certains faits' (the original has an overstrike).
'toute aussi abusive' reads 'tout(e) aussi abusive' with an overstruck letter.
Handwritten addition after 'phrase' reads 'du texte original'.
In the final line, 'Kashiwara[-s-]' carries an overstrike, followed by a long struck-out typed fragment that is illegible.
